title: Plan to Pick Presidents by Popular Vote Nears a Big Step
summary:
Imagine voting for president — and the winner did not get the most votes. That can happen because of the Electoral College. Now a plan to change that is nearing a milestone.

The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact has states give their electoral votes to the nationwide popular-vote winner. It starts once states holding 270 votes join. 18 states and the District of Columbia are in, totalling 222.

Next year Democrats will control five more states — Arizona, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Nevada and Wisconsin — with 61 votes. Four joining would pass 270. No Republican-led states have joined, but Pennsylvania's and Nevada's governors are open to signing on.

Patrick Rosenstiel of National Popular Vote has never been more confident of a national popular vote in 2028. Pew polling shows 63 percent of voters want it. But some legal experts say it could break the Constitution's compact clause, which needs Congress's permission. Norman Miller said a constitutional amendment would be safer but much harder. Opponents such as Save Our States say dropping it would push politics toward regions and deepen divides.
why_it_matters: One day you will vote, and knowing how the president is picked helps you understand why your vote matters.

keywords.explanation: The Electoral College is the system that picks the president of the United States, using votes from each state.
A milestone is an important step reached on the way to a bigger goal.
A compact is a formal agreement between states to do something together.
An amendment is a change added to a country's constitution, its most important set of rules.
Divides are splits or disagreements between groups of people.

options: The winner always gets the most votes

Give their electoral votes to the winner of their own state

background_read: In the United States, the president is chosen through the Electoral College, a system in which each state has a number of electoral votes.
That means a candidate can win the presidency without winning the most votes across the whole country.
The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact is an agreement among states to give their electoral votes to the candidate who wins the most votes nationwide.
Article_Structure: WHO: The states that have joined the compact, National Popular Vote, Patrick Rosenstiel, legal experts, and opponents such as Save Our States.
WHAT: A plan to give electoral votes to the nationwide popular-vote winner is close to the 270 votes it needs to start.
WHERE: Across the United States, in the states that have joined and the states that may join next.
WHY: Many voters want the candidate with the most votes across the country to win the presidency.
